title: Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners
description: Use verbatim methods and equipment to capture, store, retrieve, and transcribe pretrial and trial proceedings or other information. Includes stenocaptioners who operate computerized stenographic captioning equipment to provide captions of live or prerecorded broadcasts for hearing-impaired viewers.

tasks.text: Record verbatim proceedings of courts, legislative assemblies, committee meetings, and other proceedings, using computerized recording equipment, electronic stenograph machines, or stenomasks.
Proofread transcripts for correct spelling of words.
Ask speakers to clarify inaudible statements.
Provide transcripts of proceedings upon request of judges, lawyers, or the public.
Transcribe recorded proceedings in accordance with established formats.
Log and store exhibits from court proceedings.
File and store shorthand notes of court session.
File a legible transcript of records of a court case with the court clerk's office.
Verify accuracy of transcripts by checking copies against original records of proceedings and accuracy of rulings by checking with judges.
Respond to requests during court sessions to read portions of the proceedings already recorded.
Record symbols on computer storage media and use computer aided transcription to translate and display them as text.
Take notes in shorthand or use a stenotype or shorthand machine that prints letters on a paper tape.
Record depositions and other proceedings for attorneys.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Advantage Software Total Eclipse, AudioScribe SpeechCAT, Cheetah International SmartCAT, Electronic Transcript Software ProTEXT.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Acclaim Legal Acclaim DepoManage, Chase Software Solutions Court Reporting Software, Courtpages, OMTI ReporterBase.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Acculaw Court Reporters Billing Scheduling Job Management System ABSMS, ReporterWorks.
